item.title: A 'Hitchhiker's Guide' to the June 2025 ENSO update
item.description: Our blogger gives us a sci-fi themed update on the status of ENSO. Can you count all the references?
item.dc:creator: Emily Becker

item.title: Tornado season 2025: active through April, and May is keeping pace
item.description: The U.S. tornado season to date has been very active. Our guest blogger explains how the lingering influence of La Niña might have played a role.
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Malloy

item.title: May 2025 ENSO update: eye of neutral
item.description: The tropical Pacific is ENSO-neutral. Our blogger covers what that means and what forecasters expect for the rest of the year.
item.dc:creator: Emily Becker

item.title: More than just weather: how climate shapes life in Washington, D.C., and the Galapagos
item.description: Many people will say “climate is the average of weather.” That’s not wrong, but it’s not a complete explanation.
item.dc:creator: Michelle L'Heureux

item.title: April 2025 ENSO update: La Niña has ended
item.description: After just a few months, La Niña conditions have ended and the tropical Pacific has returned to neutral conditions. Our blogger gives you the scoop on La Niña's end and the forecast for the rest of…
item.dc:creator: Emily Becker

item.title: Winner or bust? Did La Niña shape North American precipitation this winter as expected?
item.description: It’s March Madness, ENSO style! Our blogger discusses why the North American precipitation pattern this past winter looked more like the response to a moderate-strength La Niña than to a weak event.
item.dc:creator: Nat Johnson

item.title: March 2025 ENSO update: neutral conditions expected soon
item.description: La Niña conditions are waning, and a transition to ENSO-neutral is favored in the next month.
item.dc:creator: Emily Becker

item.title: How good have models been at predicting ENSO in the 21st century?
item.description: A new paper looked at 20 years work of real-time ENSO Model forecasts and found some interesting patterns. Did you know models found it pretty freaking hard to predict the onset of La Nina events?
item.dc:creator: Tom Di Liberto

item.title: February 2025 La Niña update: La Niña today, gone tomorrow?
item.description: Weak La Niña conditions continued in January, but a transition to ENSO-neutral in the near future is likely.
item.dc:creator: Emily Becker

item.title: We are absolutely confident that some expected La Niña impacts will bust this winter
item.description: Why no one should expect a perfect match between what happens during a La Niña winter and the expected La Niña pattern. But knowing whether it may be a El Niño or La Niña winter is still useful!
item.dc:creator: Michelle L'Heureux
